sentences: Turn-based stochastic games combine sequential player choices, random transitions, and rewards extending over an infinite horizon.
The cited passage asks about computing exact or approximate Nash equilibria even for zero-sum games as the discount factor increases.
A discount factor approaching one makes remote future rewards increasingly relevant.
Understanding this regime would clarify whether equilibrium computation scales efficiently with a long effective planning horizon.

The saved sentence does not specify the encoding of discount factors or the approximation tolerance, both of which are necessary to distinguish polynomial complexity from parameter-dependent guarantees.
